question.text: Out of two copper spheres of the same size, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is hollow while <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></math> is solid. If they are charged at the same potential, what can be said about the charges on them?

options.text: Sphere <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> will have more charge
Sphere <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></math> will have more charge
Charge on both the spheres are equal
Charges on both the sphere are zero

solution.text:
Charges on a conductor accumulate only on the surface. Therefore, a hollow sphere or a solid one, both will have exact same charge distribution and the exact same charge for given potential.

∴   Charge on both spheres is equal.
